# MYCOBACTERIUM AVIUM PNEUMONIA

Diagnosis and treatment are complex. Regimens containing 3 or 4 drugs are usually recommended, but two drug regimens may be sufficient in some cases.
Consult Infectious Diseases and/or Pulmonary in all cases.

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treatment is continued until sputum cultures are consecutively negative for 12 months.

References:

- Mandell chapter: Mycobacterium avium Complex
- Sanford keyword: Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare
- Up-to-Date article: Treatment of Mycobacterium avium complex lung infection in adults
Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Three-drug regimens

Preferred treatment

Clarithromycin 500 mg PO q12h ($) [R,DI] <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h ($$) [R] <AND> rifabutin 300 mg PO q24h ($$) [R,DI]
Alternative
Azithromycin 250 mg PO q24h ($) M <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h [R]
<AND> rifabutin 300 mg q24h ($$) [R,DI]

Alternative
Azithromycin 250 mg PO QDay ($) M <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO QDay [R]
<AND> rifabutin 300 mg QDay ($$) [R,DI]

### Four-drug regimens may be recommended for advanced (severe) or previously treated disease-Consult Infectious Diseases

*Local guidance (St. Cloud CDSS, Inpatient):*
Diagnosis and treatment are complex.
Consult Infectious Disease for treatment recommendations

## Outpatient

### Preferred treatment

Clarithromycin 500 mg PO BID ($) [R,DI] <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO QDay ($$) [R] <AND> rifabutin 300 mg PO QDay ($$) [R,DI]

### Four-drug regimens may be recommended for advanced (severe) or previously treated disease-Consult Infectious Diseases
